correctness.rationale: A degree-five constant-width support has only frequencies 1,3,5, and the first disappears from curvature and area. With R=8 times the third-mode amplitude and S=24 times the fifth, nonnegative curvature implies the supremum of their oscillatory sum is at most w/2. At six extrema of the third harmonic, three sign-normalized sampled values are R+S cos(phi+2 pi k/3); one of those cosines is at least 1/2, giving sup >= R+S/2. The reverse-triangle estimate sup >= S-R and an exact two-regime algebraic comparison give sup squared >= R squared + S squared/2. Orthogonal Fourier integration gives area = pi w squared/4 - pi (R squared+S squared/3)/16, hence the stated 6 pi times fifth-amplitude-squared gap. Attainment of baseline forces zero fifth mode and saturated third amplitude. Those supports are convex because their curvature radius equals (w/2)(1+cos(3 theta-phi)). The standalone verifier passes 1,682 deterministic tests; the continuous assertion is proved analytically.

value.rationale: This is the natural first two-mode cutoff beyond translations for ordinary planar constant width. The exact global optimum and exhaustive arbitrary-phase equality classification rigorously resolve a fifth-degree real-cosine numerical observation from the convex optimization literature, while also furnishing a uniform quantitative penalty for fifth-harmonic amplitude. The proof distinguishes nonresonant frequency 5, which cannot lower the optimum, from the previously published resonant n:3n behavior that can lower it. The six-sample spectral lemma is structural and the coefficient-wise quadratic gap is useful for assessing finite-dimensional support-function approximations; no paper-sized consequence or globally sharp gap coefficient is claimed.
